name: self-update
description: Keeps the plugins this machine already has from the marketplaces you name current, with Claude Code's own claude plugin commands, one session at a time, and reloads each session behind an update at its next idle moment. Off until you name a marketplace. Windows only.

updateCheck.title: Update check
updateCheck.description: on: when a tool of this plugin is called and the last check is 30 minutes old, fetch this plugin's published plugin.json from GitHub (a plain GET of a public file) and say when a newer version is out. off: never check.

autoUpdate.title: Auto-update (marketplaces)
autoUpdate.description: Off unless set. Plugin marketplace names, comma-separated, such as claude-code-self-tools, example-marketplace: this machine then keeps the plugins it already has from them current. At a session's start and at each turn's end, at most once every 5 minutes for the whole machine (one session at a time, under a lock; less often, to once an hour, only while looks in a row can't reach a named marketplace), it runs Claude Code's own commands: claude plugin marketplace update <marketplace> for each named marketplace with a plugin installed here, then claude plugin update <plugin>@<marketplace> --scope <scope> for every install of it, in every scope it is installed in (a project's or a local one from its own folder). A command still running 75 s after its script started is ended with every process it started (Windows' taskkill, the one other program it runs). It never adds a marketplace, never installs a plugin that isn't installed, never touches a marketplace not named here, never asks for a version and never passes --force. Each install gets one transcript line and a toast, and, with reloadAfterUpdate on, a session whose plugins were loaded before it reloads itself at its next idle moment; a command that fails is tried again at the next look, and three looks failing in a row get one toast. A value with an entry that isn't a marketplace name's shape (letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores) turns it off, and the session says why; a name no installed plugin comes from does nothing, and a session says so once. What those marketplaces publish then runs on this machine unreviewed, and so does each listed plugin's own source (an entry can point a plugin at another repository), and whatever the marketplace's name points to on this machine now: name only marketplaces you trust that far. Windows only. One look at a time per Claude Code plugins folder.

reloadAfterUpdate.title: Reload after an update
reloadAfterUpdate.description: on: a session whose plugins were loaded before one of autoUpdate's installs runs /reload-plugins once, at a turn's end, when the session is idle (no turn running, nothing typed in the prompt box, no subagent at work, no look of its own under way), at most once every 15 minutes and at most twice for one install. off: autoUpdate only installs, and a session loads what it installed at its next start or /reload-plugins.
